request:
Source ticket: MAG-8 — https://linear.app/magus-monitor/issue/MAG-8/i18n-translations-htmx

Tier 1 of RM24-i18n-translations. The account module must own and expose the per-user language preference so the gateway can render EN/ES without ever touching the accounts table: a goose migration adding `language TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'es'` to accounts, sqlc regeneration, and an extension to the module's public port to read the current language for an account and persist a change to it. Supported values es and en, default es; an unrecognized stored value must resolve to es rather than error. No index.

decisions.decision: Database design gate CONFIRMED: `ALTER TABLE accounts ADD COLUMN language TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'es'` — no CHECK constraint, no index
decisions.why: User was shown the DDL, the index plan, and the CHECK-vs-no-CHECK trade-off and approved as designed. Vocabulary is enforced in Go at the module's sole write path (SetLanguage) and re-normalized on read, mirroring the existing unconstrained `provider` column; a CHECK would force a migration to ship ahead of the Go code when a third locale is added, for safety the single writer already provides.

decisions.decision: Accepted the worker's NOT NULL DEFAULT 'es' rather than the module's nullable access_type/vehicle_config precedent
decisions.why: Those columns are nullable because a migration cannot honestly assign a value Tesla has not reported yet. A language default has no external-observation gap — 'es' is truthful for every existing row immediately, so NOT NULL removes an unset state and a class of caller nil-handling.

decisions.decision: Accepted asymmetric language validation — reject invalid input on write, silently normalize on read
decisions.why: Roadmap Decision #4 requires that an invalid stored value never break a render, which demands read-side normalization; a caller passing a bad code live is a different failure that should surface as ErrUnsupportedLanguage rather than be silently swallowed.

decisions.decision: Batched all 15 tasks into ONE serial worker dispatch instead of 8 dependency-ordered waves
decisions.why: The graph is effectively a chain (T1.1->T3.1->T3.3->T4.1->T5/T7); max real parallelism is 2-3 trivial tasks. Eight dispatches would each re-read the same 4-file doc pack, costing far more than the parallelism saves on a single-module change this small.

decisions.decision: Dispatched on Sonnet rather than Opus
decisions.why: Single-module change with a complete approved design.md and 15 atomic tasks; no cross-cutting or ambiguous work. Sonnet is the skill's default and Opus would need a justified exception.

decisions.decision: Leader fixed the two cross-module fakeAccount test doubles (gateway/handlers, telemetry) rather than re-dispatching the worker
decisions.why: Widening account.Service broke consumers' test doubles outside the worker's sandbox. That is leader-owned cross-module integration code; the worker correctly blocked T7.1/T7.2/T7.4 instead of reaching out of its module. Both stubs are inert and return LanguageES rather than "" so no existing test's behaviour changes.
